sources.title: Cisco Packet Tracer 7.0 Frequently Asked Questions
sources.notes: Document title and Last Updated date are in the mirrored Cisco Public Information content. Q5 explicitly identifies 829,1240 and IE2000 as New Devices. Earlier-family absence is an inference from introduction, not a runtime observation.

sources.title: Cisco Networking Academy September 2017 Program Updates: Packet Tracer 7.1 Overview
sources.notes: Cisco copyright presentation, Packet Tracer 7.1 Overview slide 18 explicitly describes CT2504 WLC and 3702 APs as new devices; release available August 2017. Earlier-family absence is inferred from introduction. CT2504 and 3702 map to catalogue WLC-2504 and 3702i.

sources.title: Cisco Packet Tracer 7.2.2 bundled help: What's New
sources.notes: Original English Cisco help mirrored at https://github.com/Yue-plus/cisco_packet_tracer_help. README names the Cisco Packet Tracer 7.2.2 install directory and default/menu.htm links PacketTracer722v10.pdf. New Devices lists Meraki Security Appliance, Home Router and ASA5506. Corresponding help identifies Meraki-MX65W. ASA5506 is the help label for catalogue ASA5506-X. Exact original introduction minor is not asserted.

sources.title: Cisco Packet Tracer help: What's New in version 9.0
sources.notes: Explicitly calls C8200 a new router model and lists IR1101,IR8340,IE3400 and ISA3000 under New in version9.0. Earlier-family absence is an inference from introduction, not an observation of old runtimes.

sources.title: Devices and Modules: Routers
sources.notes: Online 9.0 help corroborated against C:/Program Files/Cisco Packet Tracer 9.0.1/help/default/devicesAndModules_routers.htm. Installed documentation identifies the exact observed package release as 9.0.1; no simulator behavior was executed.

sources.title: Devices and Modules: Switches
sources.notes: Online 9.0 help corroborated against the identically named installed 9.0.1 help page. Category inventory is not treated as exhaustive evidence of absence.

sources.title: Devices and Modules: Other Devices
sources.notes: Online 9.0 help corroborated against the identically named installed 9.0.1 help page. The ASA heading is ASA 5506, without the -X suffix.

sources.title: What's New in Cisco Packet Tracer 9.0
sources.notes: Explicit New in version 9.0 list includes IR1101, IR8340, PT8200, IE3400 and ISA3000. The introduction describes the C8200 router addition and the linked inventory calls it PT8200. Earlier-major absence is an inference, not a directly observed 8.x inventory.

sources.title: enable dhcpd in ASA5506-X firewall
sources.notes: Original reporter explicitly names ASA5506-X in Packet Tracer 9.0 and says the same DHCP configuration works in 8.2. A reply explicitly identifies 9.0.0 and copying an ASA from PT-8. User-generated firsthand evidence, not an official supported-device inventory.

Exact file SHA256 6cd2b8891df92d2cad8b6fdc47480fc089de085c4f3fe95eb80d5450a2a7f72d; SHA512 55835357b01449150f5c962d852f2921d4e39f697297cb34471b8cc83a91bced6c31703cc28a90e61db7a9a32e5534de4f11e5c4f6735f400456d25a013fadde matches independently maintained AUR PKGBUILD at commit 400c3e5dce781938bea6b5131d26effed7f7c3cc (https://aur.archlinux.org/cgit/aur.git/tree/PKGBUILD?h=packettracer&id=400c3e5dce781938bea6b5131d26effed7f7c3cc). Reviewed opt/pt/help/default/devicesAndModules_routers.htm, devicesAndModules_switches.htm, devicesAndModules_others.htm and whatsNew.htm. These resources alone do not prove active palette behavior.
